BA.rationale: Boeing's duopoly franchise and massive $545-695B backlog provide structural moat, and the operational turnaround under CEO Ortberg is gaining traction — Q1 2026 operating income of $448M (filing data, correcting the $380M cited in secondary sources) and revenue up 14% YoY represent a genuine inflection from deep losses. Delivery rates are accelerating (60 aircraft in May 2026, +33% YoY) and the FAA has raised the 737 MAX production cap to 47/month. Global Services at 18.1% margins with a $33B backlog is an underappreciated earnings lever. However, the balance sheet remains severely strained with $47B in debt and only $6B equity, 777X delays have consumed $15B+ in charges, active 737 MAX litigation creates legal overhang, and forward P/E of ~40x for 2026 prices in substantial recovery that must still be delivered. Normalized FCF of ~$6B is not expected until 2027. The China 200-jet order disappointed expectations. This is a credible multi-year turnaround story with real franchise value, but the wide confidence interval on cash-flow normalization timing and leverage risk cap the score at mildly attractive. No strong near-term catalyst to push higher.
key_factors: Q1 2026 operating income $448M (filing data) — first positive quarter after multiple deep-loss quarters; revenue $22.22B up 14% YoY
Duopoly franchise with 6,700+ plane backlog ($545-695B); Boeing outsold Airbus in 2025 (1,175 vs 1,000 gross orders) for first time since 2018
Delivery acceleration: 60 commercial aircraft in May 2026 (+33% YoY); FAA raised 737 MAX production cap to 47/month from 42/month
Global Services: $5.4B Q1 revenue (+6% YoY), 18.1% operating margin, record $33B backlog — structural growth lever
Balance sheet strain: $46.96B total debt (Q1 2026) vs $5.99B equity; constrains capital allocation and leaves no margin for execution error
777X delays to 2027 with $15B+ in accumulated charges; cash neutrality targeted 2028, positive FCF from 2029 on this program
Active 737 MAX litigation: LOT Polish Airlines jury trial in Seattle — first airline lawsuit tied to MAX crashes to reach public courtroom
China 200-jet order secured but market expected larger deal; stock fell on announcement
Forward P/E ~40x for 2026 (simplywall.st) prices in substantial recovery; normalized FCF ~$6B not expected until 2027
Airbus still leads in deliveries: 793 vs 600 in 2025, 262 vs 250 YTD through May 2026 — Boeing can sell but cannot yet build at competitive rates
